answer.reason: Several passages tell of things that happened at or to Tyre: its king supplying David, the prophecy of its fall, and Jesus entering its coasts.

clauses.english: sent cedar trees, carpenters and masons to build David a house
clauses.quote: sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons

clauses.english: was foretold to fall to Nebuchadrezzar and be made like the top of a rock
clauses.quote: I will bring upon Tyrus Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon

clauses.english: was visited by Jesus, who went into its coasts
clauses.quote: Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

doubts: Verses naming Hiram the brass-worker, a man of Tyre (1KI 7:13-14), and the verses on the king of Tyre's gifts to Solomon concern other persons or repeat the same help, so they were left out.
The Ezekiel 28 verses addressed to the prince and king of Tyre were not used, since they are rebuke and lamentation, not events.
Joshua 19:29 and 2 Samuel 24:7 only list Tyre among places and were not used.
